ATOPIC DERMATITIS (eczema) is part of the “atopic” patient syndrome
which includes asthma, alopecia (hair loss), and lowered immune response.
This syndrome is one of malabsorption of essential fatty acids

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000159.claim_text: Wallach explains that the positive 'sweat test' used to diagnose cystic fibrosis is the result of an essential fatty acid deficiency. That deficiency causes a secondary shortage of prostaglandins — very short-lived hormones — which normally control the sodium, chloride, and potassium levels of the sweat. He presents the abnormal sweat chemistry as tracing back to a fatty-acid deficiency.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000159.verbatim:
It has been learned recently that the positive “sweat test” is the result of an
essential fatty acid deficiency that causes a secondary deficiency of
“prostaglandin” (very short lived hormones) that control the sodium,
chlorides, and potassium levels of the sweat!!!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000160.claim_text: Wallach breaks with the idea that acne is just a teenage hormone or hygiene problem: he calls it primarily the result of an essential fatty acid deficiency, made worse by eating too much saturated and damaged polyunsaturated fat — the kind in fried foods and margarine. His fix is to cut the fast food, supply the missing good fats (essential fatty acids at about 3% of daily calories, or 9 grams a day), and check for food allergies, rather than reaching first for antibiotics.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000160.verbatim:
Acne is primarily the result of an essential
fatty acid deficiency with a concurrent intake of too much saturated fat and
polyunsaturated fatty acids (fried foods and margarine).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000161.claim_text: Wallach tells people to pay special attention to their essential fatty acids while avoiding as much of the other polyunsaturated fats as they can, naming flaxseed oil and/or salmon oil as 'the essentials' to consume. In his heart-disease guidance these two oils are the go-to sources, set apart from the polyunsaturated oils he warns against.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000161.verbatim:
Pay special attention to EFA, avoid as much of
the polyunsaturated fatty acids as you can (other than the essentials— i.e.
flaxseed oil and/or salmon oil)

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000162.claim_text: Wallach treats dry skin — along with cracked cuticles, hangnails, and a cracked index finger and thumb — as more than a cosmetic issue: he calls it a signal of essential fatty acid deficiency that can result in cardiovascular disease such as thrombosis, stroke, and heart attack. He warns that the deeper consequences of this deficiency can be sudden and deadly, and coins the shorthand 'DSM/EFA,' meaning 'dry skin means essential fatty acids.'
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000162.verbatim:
DRY SKIN (cracked cuticles, hang nails, cracked
index finger and thumb) is a common malady in the western world. In itself,
it is a cosmetic problem. It is a signal of a potentially more serious problem
— essential fatty acid deficiency that can result in cardiovascular disease
(i.e.—thrombosis, stroke, heart attack, etc.). Superficial creams will
temporarily deal with the superficial problem, but the more ominous results
of the body’s deficiency of essential fatty acids can be sudden and deadly!!!
DSM/EFA or “dry skin means essential fatty acids”!!!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000163.claim_text: In his home-care first-aid entry for abrasions, Wallach recommends taking vitamin C orally 'to bowel tolerance,' which he gives as anywhere from 1 to 5 grams.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000163.verbatim:
ABRASIONS (scrapes): clean wounds with soap and water to remove
gross dirt and debris. Disinfect wounds with H2O2 (hydrogen peroxide).
Wounds may be bathed in a variety of herbal washes or poultice. Our choice
is aloe, plantain (Plantago major), or comfrey (Symphytum officinale).
Colloidal silver is useful here. Take Vitamin C orally to bowel tolerance
(anywhere from 1-5 grams).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000164.claim_text: In his multiple sclerosis protocol, Wallach makes an exception to his usual high-dose vitamin C advice: he recommends avoiding large doses of vitamin C supplementation and instead eating green vegetables and juices as a natural source of vitamin C. He notes the same treatment regimen has proved effective for ALS (Lou Gehrig's Disease). This is a distinctive, condition-specific caution rather than general guidance.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000164.verbatim:
avoid large doses of vitamin C
supplementation. Eat green vegetables and juices as a natural source of
vitamin C.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000165.claim_text: Wallach teaches that night blindness (xerophthalmia) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency, which can arise several ways. It can come from an outright dietary shortage, from fat-malabsorption syndromes (vitamin A is fat-soluble), or from a zinc deficiency that leaves the liver unable to convert carotene into vitamin A. Conditions such as cystic fibrosis, celiac disease, and food allergies that damage the intestine and block absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, as well as a lack of essential fatty acids, can also cause it. He treats night blindness very specifically with 25,000 to 300,000 IU of vitamin A per day as beta-carotene plus zinc at 15 to 50 mg three times a day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000165.verbatim:
NIGHT BLINDNESS (xerophthalmia) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency
which can be overt dietary deficiency, fat malabsorption syndrome (vitamin
A is fat soluble), zinc deficiency which results in poor conversion of
carotene to vitamin A by the liver, cystic fibrosis, celiac disease and various
food allergies resulting in intestinal changes that prevent absorption of fat
soluble vitamins (i.e. vitamin A, vitamin E, vitamin D and vitamin K), as
well as a deficiency of essential fatty acids.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000166.claim_text: Wallach identifies 'shark skin' (keratosis) as a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc, usually resulting from a low-animal-protein diet. It shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth (cheilosis), oral lesions often secondarily infected with Candida, a 'geographic' tongue, and skin lesions with hard granular plugs of sebaceous and keratinized material in the hair follicles that give a sandpaper-like surface.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000166.verbatim:
SHARK SKIN (keratosis) is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc
(usually as a result of low animal protein diets). Shark skin is characterized
by cracks in the corners of the mouth (cheilosis), oral lesions that are often
secondarily infected by Candida albicans (per
leche), “geographic” tongue, and skin lesions characterized by hard
granular plugs resulting from collections of sebaceous and keratinized
material in hair follicles which gives a sandpaper-like surface (shark skin).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000167.claim_text: For cancer therapy programs, Wallach says beta-carotene taken together with vitamin E can be used at as much as 600,000 IU of vitamin A equivalent. He considers this of significant benefit, especially for carcinomas. He adds that the vitamin A provided this way also helps the thymus gland produce antibodies and makes laetrile more effective.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000167.verbatim:
Beta-carotene taken with vitamin E can be taken at as much as 600,000 IU
vitamin A equivalent! This will be of significant benefit in cancer therapy
programs, especially CARCINOMAS. The vitamin A thus provided will
also help the thymus gland produce antibodies and make laetrile more
effective.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000168.claim_text: For acne, Wallach recommends a regimen of vitamin A at 300,000 units per day as beta-carotene for five months, then reducing to 25,000 per day. He pairs it with vitamin B6 at 100 mg three times a day and zinc at 50 mg three times a day for 30 days, and suggests vitamin E oil applied topically to the acne lesions. He treats acne primarily as an essential-fatty-acid problem, so this vitamin A protocol sits on top of correcting fats and food allergies.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000168.verbatim:
A regimen of Vitamin A 300,000 units/day (as beta-carotene)
for five months, then reduce to 25,000 i per day B6 100 mg t.i.d., zinc 50
mg t.i.d. for 30 days, and vitamin E oil may be applied topically to acne
lesions is also recommended.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000169.claim_text: Wallach describes keratomalacia (xerophthalmia) as a hazy, 'bluish,' dry cornea, the clear dome on the front of the eye, that becomes ulcerated. Its symptoms include extreme dryness of the eyes with constant blinking to keep them moist, conjunctivitis, and night blindness, and fat-like 'Bitot's spots' can appear on the white of the eyeball. He warns that untreated keratomalacia can result in permanent blindness.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000169.verbatim:
KERATOMALACIA (xerophthalmia) is recognized as a hazy “bluish” dry
cornea (the domed clear bulge on the front of the eye) that becomes
ulcerated. Symptoms include extreme dryness of the eyes with blinking in
attempts to keep the eyes moist, conjunctivitis, and night blindness. Fat-like
spots (Bitots spots) can be found on the “white” of the eyeball. Untreated
keratomalacia can result in permanent blindness.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000170.claim_text: Wallach teaches that miscarriage (spontaneous abortion) is usually caused by deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals, and/or protein. In particular, he names vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium, and complete proteins as essential to maintaining a pregnancy. This places adequate vitamin A among the key nutrients a mother needs to carry a healthy pregnancy to term.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000170.verbatim:
MISCARRIAGE (spontaneous abortion) is
usually due to deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals, and/or protein. In
particular, vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium, and complete proteins are
essential to maintenance of pregnancy.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000172.claim_text: Wallach teaches that rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D and is marked by stunted growth, joint pain, and deformed long bones such as bow legs, dropped wrists, sickle shins, barrel chest, and rachitic rosary. His treatment is supplementation with vitamin D at 400 IU orally twice a day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per day. Advanced cases may still require orthotic correction or orthopedic surgery.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000172.verbatim:
RICKETS is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D and is characterized by
stunted growth, joint pain, and deformed long bones (i.e. bow legs, dropped
wrists, “sickle shins,” barrel chest, rachitic rosary, etc.).
Treatment of rickets includes supplementation with vitamin D at 400 IU
orally b.i.d., calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day,
and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000173.claim_text: Wallach places iron storage disease and iron-resistant anemia among the symptoms of copper deficiency, alongside signs such as crow's feet, skin wrinkles, spider and varicose veins, hemorrhoids, and liver cirrhosis. In his framework these iron-labeled problems are actually signs of a copper shortage, not of iron itself.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000173.verbatim:
Additional symptoms of copper deficiency
include crow’s feet, skin wrinkles, spider veins, varicose veins,
hemorrhoids, liver cirrhosis, iron storage disease, and iron resistant anemia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000174.claim_text: Wallach describes calcium as essential to all living organisms and the fifth most abundant mineral in the earth's crust and biosphere. It is also the most abundant mineral in the human body: about 99 percent of it forms the hydroxyapatite crystal that gives bones and teeth their structure, while the remaining one percent works as a cofactor and activator — regulating the electrochemical functions of cells, releasing energy from ATP (adenosine triphosphate) for muscle contraction, driving blood clotting, triggering neurotransmitter release, and helping regulate the heartbeat. He argues that humans are biochemically designed for high-calcium diets, that modern American diets are critically deficient in it, and that supplementation is the only practical way to get enough.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000174.verbatim:
Calcium is essential for all organisms and is found in the cell walls of
plants, all calcareous tissues, and mammalian bones. Calcium also helps
regulate electrochemical functions in cells and activates several enzymes.
Calcium is the fifth most abundant mineral element in the earth’s crust and
biosphere.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000175.claim_text: According to Wallach, causes of calcium deficiency include a lack of vitamin D and a deficiency of stomach acid — the low stomach acid (hypochlorhydria) itself often stemming from a salt-restricted diet. Lactose intolerance, celiac disease, high-fat diets, low protein intake, and high phytate consumption also lead to deficiency. In the same discussion he notes phytic acid in grain bran binds calcium into unabsorbable calcium phytate, oxalic acid in foods like spinach and rhubarb forms unabsorbable calcium oxalate, and dietary fiber itself prevents calcium absorption.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000175.verbatim:
Causes of calcium deficiency include a lack of vitamin D. So does a
deficiency of stomach acid. Often the lack of stomach acid or
hypochlorhydria results from a restricted NaCl (salt) intake. Lactose
intolerance, celiac disease, high fat diet, and low protein intake and high
phytate consumption can lead to calcium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000176.claim_text: Wallach explains that bone matrix — the gelatinous, collagen-based foundation of bone — makes up 25 to 40 percent of total bone weight (about 40 percent in children and 25 percent in adults). Without this gelatinous matrix, most newly supplemented calcium cannot be retained in the bones, and most of what is absorbed is simply urinated out of the body. This is why his approach pairs calcium with the collagen, glucosamine, and chondroitin that form the building blocks of bone and cartilage.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000176.verbatim:
Bone matrix is the gelatinous foundation of bone. Bone matrix makes up as
much as 25 to 40 percent of the total bone weight, depending upon the age
of the individual—40 percent in kids and 25 percent in adults. Without the
gelatinous bone matrix, most new supplemental calcium could not be
retained in bones and most of what is absorbed is just urinated out of the
body.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000177.claim_text: Wallach explains that calcium and magnesium play antagonistic roles in normal muscle contraction: calcium is the stimulator and magnesium is the relaxer. An excess of magnesium will inhibit bone calcification, while an excessive amount of calcium can induce the signs of magnesium deficiency. This balance is why his supplement protocols consistently pair the two minerals rather than giving calcium alone.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000177.verbatim:
AN EXCESS OF
MAGNESIUM WILL INHIBIT BONE CALCIFICATION. Calcium and
Mg have antagonistic roles in normal muscle contraction, calcium acting as
the stimulator and Mg as the relaxer. An excessive amount of Ca can induce
signs of Mg deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000178.claim_text: Wallach observes that Chinese cuisine includes no dairy products — no cheese dishes — yet Chinese people require calcium like everyone else, and he found they get it from animal bones. He describes his wife, Ma Lan, simmering the bones of fish, chicken, pork, and beef in a vinegar solution, which leaches calcium, magnesium, manganese, boron, copper, sulfur, and other minerals out of the bones into the soup. The example illustrates his point that dairy is not the only or necessary source of dietary calcium.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000178.verbatim:
As a culture the Chinese
do not eat dairy products. It’s just not part of their cuisine, yet they require
calcium like all other humans. If you go to a Chinese restaurant, there are
no cheese dishes. I often wondered where the Chinese people got their
calcium. They get their calcium from animal bones.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000179.claim_text: Wallach argues the entire scope of American diets is critically deficient in calcium, and that the only practical way to get enough is through supplementation. He is sharply critical of the researchers who, instead of recommending effective calcium supplements, told people to eat five cups of broccoli a day as a calcium source — noting how impractical that is, especially for children. He counts no fewer than 147 deficiency diseases attributable to calcium shortfall or imbalance.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000179.verbatim:
There are no less than 147 deficiency diseases that can be attributed to
calcium deficiencies or imbalances. The most recent clinical research
clearly points out that the entire scope of American diets are critically
deficient in calcium. The only practical way to get enough calcium is
through supplementation. Interestingly, the allopathic physicians who did
the study failed in their duty. Instead of simply recommending effective
calcium supplementation, they recommended eating five cups of broccoli a
day as a valuable source of calcium. Try and get a kid to eat that!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000180.claim_text: Wallach teaches that the ideal calcium-to-phosphorus (Ca:P) ratio in the daily diet should be 2:1, but that this is not possible by eating food alone. American soils and food are deficient in calcium while the diet is rich in phosphorus, which is in almost everything eaten. He drives the point home with an example: to balance a 16-ounce steak you would have to eat 25 pounds of broccoli — making calcium supplementation, plus cutting high-phosphorus items like colas, the only practical way to approach the 2:1 ideal.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000180.verbatim:
Not only are our soils and food deficient in calcium, additionally the
American diet is rich in phosphorous, which is found in just about
everything we eat. Ideally, the calcium to phosphorous (or Ca:P) ratio in our
daily diet should be 2:1. This ideal ratio is not possible by simply eating
food. You would have to eat 25 pounds of broccoli every time you ate a 16
oz. steak!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000181.claim_text: Wallach argues there is clear evidence humans are designed to consume high-calcium diets, pointing to the late Paleolithic (35,000 to 10,000 years ago) as the last time humans lived in the environment they were biochemically designed for. The agricultural revolution 10,000 years ago narrowed the variety of wild foods while raising calorie intake, permanently lowering dietary minerals, trace minerals, and rare earths. Wild plants and game would have supplied Stone Age humans roughly 1,600 mg of calcium at rest and 2,000–3,000 mg at working energy levels, whereas 20th-century American adults take in only one-fifth to one-third as much — a median of 300–508 mg a day for women and just 680 mg for men.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000181.verbatim:
There is evidence that clearly shows humans are designed to
consume and use high calcium diets. The late Paleolithic period of 35,000
to 10,000 years ago was the most recent time that our human forebears
lived in the environment for which they had been biochemically designed.
The agricultural revolution occurred 10,000 years ago and it reduced the
wide variety of wild foods in the human food chain while increased food
energy (calories). These dietary changes universally and forever decreased
man’s dietary intake of minerals, trace minerals, and rare earths. The
uncultivated food plants and wild game commonly available to Stone Age
humans would supply 1600 mg at basal energy intakes and between 2,000
and 3,000 mg of calcium at the energy levels required to support hunting
and work.
During the 20th century, American adults have a calcium intake of only
one-fifth to one-third as much as did Stone Age humans. The National
Health & Nutrition Examination Survey II reported a median calcium
intake for American women of between 300 and 508 mg per day and only
680 mg for men.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000182.claim_text: Wallach recounts that as a teenager troubled by cramping and twitching eyelids, he found in library health books that the cause was listed as a calcium deficiency. Knowing the calf pellets stored in his family's barn were loaded with calcium, he filled his pockets and ate them at school while classmates ate jellybeans and M&Ms. Within four days the cramps and twitches in his eyelids went away, and he realized at age fourteen that doctors knew little or nothing about nutrition.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000182.verbatim:
I knew where we had calcium. The calf pellets stored in the barn were
loaded with calcium. I ran home and filled the pockets of my shirt, jeans,
and jacket with calf pellets. The next day in school while everyone else was
eating jellybeans and M & M’s, I was, without shame, eating calf pellets. In
four days the cramps and twitches in my eyelids went away. I realized that
day, at age fourteen, that doctors knew little or nothing about nutrition.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000183.claim_text: Korsakoff's syndrome is a recent-memory loss that Wallach calls a 'false Alzheimer's disease,' characterized by an inability to record and store new memories — the patient can still perform tasks learned before onset but cannot learn the simplest new ones. It can result from a blow to the head or from chronic alcoholism together with vitamin B1 deficiency, associated with an excess intake of simple carbohydrate and sugar. Confabulation — producing imaginary experiences to fill in what cannot be recalled — is a consistent feature.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000183.verbatim:
KORSAKOFF’S SYNDROME (recent memory loss, false Alzheimer’s
Disease) is characterized by an inability to record and store new memory.
The patient can perform detailed tasks learned before onset but cannot learn
the simplest of new tasks. This type of “amnesia” can result from a blow to
the head or be the result of chronic alcoholism and vitamin B1 deficiency
associated with an excess intake of simple carbohydrate and sugar.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000184.claim_text: Wallach describes freshwater dolphins that were fed exclusively on frozen smelt. Smelt muscle tissue contains a significant amount of the enzyme thiaminase, which more than cancelled out any thiamine (vitamin B1) the dolphins received from their daily vitamin supplement. While cooking deactivates such enzymes in raw meat, the dolphins of course did not cook their food, so a deficiency developed. The state was solved by immediately changing the diet to thiaminase-free fish plus added thiamine.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000184.verbatim:
The dolphins’ diet consisted exclusively of frozen smelt. Smelt muscle
tissue contains a significant amount of thiaminase enzyme that was more
than canceling out any thiamin the dolphin received from their daily
vitamin supplement. While cooking deactivates the enzymes of raw meat,
obviously dolphins don’t cook their food.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000185.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, cheilosis — also called angular stomatitis — is the result of a vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency. The deficiency shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth, in the nasolabial folds beside the nose, and as a 'geographic' tongue. He treats it by first identifying food allergies and then supplementing riboflavin.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000185.verbatim:
CHEILOSIS (angular stomatitis) is the result of vitamin B2 or riboflavin
deficiency. The deficiency shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth,
nasolabial folds, and “geographic” tongue.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000186.claim_text: For cheilosis — the cracked mouth corners of riboflavin deficiency — Wallach's treatment is supplementation with vitamin B2 at 75 mg taken three times a day (t.i.d.), together with identifying any contributing food allergies.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000186.verbatim:
Treatment of cheilosis includes identification of food allergies and
supplementation with B2 at 75 mg t.i.d.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000187.claim_text: For elevated cholesterol, Wallach's treatment centers on regular exercise and the baseline supplement program, with oat bran or protein fiber and vitamin C to bowel tolerance. It specifically includes niacin at 450 mg twice a day in time-release form, along with essential fatty acids at 5 g three times a day, calcium and magnesium, chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg each, and selenium at 300 mcg.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000187.verbatim:
Treatment for elevated cholesterol includes regular exercise, base line
supplement program, one to two heaping tablespoons of oat bran or protein
fiber (soy powder) in an eight oz. glass of juice, vitamin C to bowel
tolerance, essential fatty acids at 5 gm t.i.d., niacin at 450 mg b.i.d. as time
release tablets, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day,
chromium at 250 mcg., vanadium 250 mcg, selenium at 300 mcg., and
herbs to include evening primrose (Oenothera biennis).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000188.claim_text: Wallach holds that there is considerable evidence schizophrenia is the result of a severe niacin deficiency. He notes the very word 'megavitamin' was coined to describe the large dose — about 4,000 mg per day — of niacin required to 'cure' a schizophrenic.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000188.verbatim:
SCHIZOPHRENIA (“split” personality): see bi-polar brain disease. There
is considerable evidence to show that schizophrenia is the result of a severe
niacin deficiency. The term “megavitamin” was coined to describe the large
dose (4,000 mg/day) of niacin required to “cure” a schizophrenic.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000189.claim_text: According to Wallach, vitamin B6 alone will frequently 'cure' epilepsy when taken at 50 to 100 mg three times a day. He notes that long-term administration can cause some numbness and tingling in the face or hands. He presents this as a nutritional route contrasted with the anticonvulsant drugs (like phenytoin and phenobarbital) he criticizes for their dramatic and potentially dangerous side effects.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000189.verbatim:
Vitamin B6 alone will frequently “cure” epilepsy at 50-100
mg ti.d.. Long-term administration can cause some numbness and tingling
in the face or hands.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000190.claim_text: Wallach treats alcoholism as an addictive allergy complicated by hypoglycemia and vitamin/mineral malnutrition. His protocol includes vitamin B6 at 100 mg twice a day, alongside calcium, magnesium, essential fatty acids, and chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg a day, which he says are essential to solve the underlying hypoglycemia.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000190.verbatim:
Take calcium (2000 mg) and magnesium
(1000 mg) per day, essential fatty acids 5 mg t.i.d. Vitamin B6 100 mg
b.i.d., and chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg/day are essential to solve
the hypoglycemia problem.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000191.claim_text: Wallach describes meningocele (severe anencephaly or spina bifida) as a birth defect caused by a deficiency of folic acid, B12, or zinc and vitamin A during early pregnancy, often the result of deficient diets or malabsorption in the mother. He points to a large cluster of anencephaly babies born to migrant workers in McAllen, Texas in the early 1990s: public health authorities attributed it to a chemical pollutant, but Wallach argues it actually appears to be a folic acid and zinc deficiency from the winter diet of poor migrant workers living on corn tortillas. He urges all women of childbearing age to take the 90 essential nutrients before, during, and after pregnancy.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000191.verbatim:
This
birth defect is caused by a deficiency of folic acid, B12, or zinc and vitamin
A during early pregnancy. These deficiencies may be the result of deficient
diets and/or malabsorption syndromes in the pregnant mother. Severe cases
may be debilitating or fatal. A large cluster of anencephila babies born to
migrant workers occurred in McAllen, Texas in the early 90s. This cluster is
thought by public health authorities to be due to some chemical pollutant. It
actually appears to be a folic acid and zinc deficiency in the winter diet of
poor migrant workers living on corn tortillas.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000192.claim_text: For anemia — a lack of red blood cells from causes including hemorrhage, infection, and nutritional deficiency — Wallach's regimen features folic acid at 15 mg for 20 days. It is combined with betaine HCl before meals to assure B12 absorption, plus liver extract, iron at 20 mg/day, B12 at 1,000 mcg/day for 20 days, copper, zinc, B2, B5, B6, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, vitamin E, selenium, and essential fatty acids. Folic acid is one of the core blood-building nutrients in his anemia protocol.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000192.verbatim:
ANEMIA is a lack of red blood cells from many
possible causes including hemorrhage, infections, and/or nutritional
deficiencies. Betaine HCl orally at 75-200 mg t.i.d. 15-20 minutes before
meals is required to assure absorption of B12, liver extract orally or IM,
nutritional support with iron 20 mg per day, B12 1000 mcg per day for 20
days, folic acid 15 mg for 20 days, copper 2 mg, zinc 50 mg t.i.d., B-2 50
mg b.i.d., B-5 50 mg t.i.d., B-6 50 mg b.i.d. for 20 days, vitamin C to bowel
tolerance, vitamin E 800-1200 IU per day, selenium 500 mcg/day, and
essential fatty acids at a rate of 9 grams per day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000193.claim_text: Vitamin B12 travels through an enterohepatic circulation, a recycling loop that pulls B12 back from bile and other intestinal secretions and returns it to the liver. This conservation is why B12 deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after they give up meat. On top of that, the body can store up to 2 mg of B12, releasing it slowly to the bone marrow as needed; any excess beyond storage capacity is simply shed in the urine, which Wallach dryly calls 'expensive urine.'
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000193.verbatim:
There is an enterohepatic (intestine direct to the
liver) circulation of Vitamin B12 that recycles B12 from bile and other
intestinal secretions which explains why B12 deficiency in vegans may not
appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.
The maximum storage level of B12 is 2 mg, which is slowly released to the
bone marrow as needed. Excess intake of B12 above the body’s storage
capacity is shed in the urine (expensive urine).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000194.claim_text: One of Wallach's formative lessons came from his professor Boyd Odell, who in 1956 created spina bifida in laboratory animals simply by feeding the pregnant mothers diets deficient in zinc, vitamin B12, and folic acid. This showed that many so-called 'genetic' birth defects are really nutritional deficiencies. It is the basis for Wallach's concept of preconception nutrition: supplying the right nutrients before conception could prevent up to 98% of such birth defects in animals.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000194.verbatim:
He created spina bifida in laboratory animals in
1956 by feeding the pregnant mothers with diets deficient in zinc, vitamin
B12, and folic acid.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000195.claim_text: Wallach identifies the primary cause of hemorrhoids as a copper deficiency, which breaks down the elastic fibers in the walls of veins. He lists low-fiber diets, the resulting constipation, and lack of exercise as additional contributors, but treats the weakened, ballooning veins as fundamentally a connective-tissue problem rooted in too little copper.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000195.verbatim:
The cause of hemorrhoids is primarily a copper deficiency (a
breakdown of elastic fibers in veins), low fiber diets, the resulting
constipation, and lack of exercise.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000196.claim_text: Wallach states that when people supplement with plant-derived colloidal copper, their original hair color can come back, spider veins, varicose veins, and hemorrhoids can go away, and some aneurysms can even heal. He presents graying and these vein problems as reversible consequences of a copper deficiency rather than permanent effects of aging.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000196.verbatim:
When humans supplement with plant derived
colloidal copper, their original hair color can come back, spider veins,
varicose veins, and hemorrhoids can go away and some aneurysms can
heal.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000197.claim_text: Wallach holds that aneurysms are most frequently caused by copper deficiency, which weakens the elastic fibers in artery walls. While copper supplementation may not cure or repair every aneurysm, he says it can prevent them when taken at 2 to 4 mg per day and properly absorbed. Surgery is still needed for most existing aneurysms, but he cites evidence that arterial elastic fibers can be repaired with copper and reports one aortic aneurysm that was corrected with copper supplementation and confirmed by x-ray.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000197.verbatim:
Aneurysms are most frequently caused by copper
deficiency which results in weakened elastic fibers. While copper
supplementation may not “cure” or repair all aneurysm, it can prevent them
when supplemented at the rate of 2-4 mg/day if it is being properly absorbed.
Surgery will be required for most existing aneurysms, although there is a
considerable amount of evidence to show that arterial elastic fibers can be
repaired by supplementing diets with copper. We do have one aortic
aneurysm that has been corrected with copper supplementation and
confirmed by x-ray.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000198.claim_text: For joint pain, Wallach's program includes copper at 2 to 5 mg per day and notes that a copper bracelet can be of great value. He treats the bracelet as a genuine route of copper absorption rather than folklore, placing copper alongside calcium and magnesium, cartilage, gelatin, and B6 in his joint-pain protocol.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000198.verbatim:
cartilage at 5 gm t.i.d., gelatin (unsweetened) once per day,
copper at 2-5 mg/day (a copper bracelet can be of great value), B6 at 100
mg t.i.d.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000199.claim_text: Wallach challenges the orthodox view that Menkes kinky hair syndrome is a genetic disease, describing it instead as a malabsorption problem in early infancy, such as celiac disease, that results in a copper deficiency along with other deficiencies. He notes it has long been known in veterinary medicine that copper deficiency causes 'kinky wool' disease. His treatment addresses the malabsorption first, avoiding wheat, cow's milk, and soy and adding digestive enzymes and betaine HCl, then gives copper IV at 200 ug/kg/day and copper orally at 1 to 2 mg per day after symptoms relieve.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000199.verbatim:
MENKE’S KINKY HAIR SYNDROME is thought by the “orthodox”
pediatrician to be a genetic disease, but it appears to be a malabsorption
problem in early infancy (i.e. celiac disease) that results in a copper
deficiency (along with other deficiencies). It has long been known in the
veterinary field that a copper deficiency causes “kinky wool” disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000200.claim_text: Chromium's blood-sugar role runs through a specific molecule Wallach describes: the glucose tolerance factor, or GTF, a complex of trivalent chromium (chromium III), dinicotinic acid (a form of niacin), and glutathione. In that form chromium activates phosphoglucomutase and other enzymes that let the body process glucose — which is why he treats chromium, not insulin alone, as central to blood-sugar control. He notes the whole body holds only about 1.5 mg of it.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000200.verbatim:
Chromium activates phosphoglucomutase and other enzymes and is
closely associated with GTF or glucose tolerance factor. GTF is a
combination of chromium III, dinicotinic acid, and glutathione.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000201.claim_text: Wallach explains that dietary sugar loads — colas, apple juice, grape juice, honey, candy, table sugar, and fructose — increase the natural rate of urinary chromium loss by 300 percent for 12 hours. Because sugar flushes chromium out through the urine, a high-sugar diet drives the very deficiency that impairs blood-sugar control. This is part of why he ties sugar consumption to diabetes and hypoglycemia.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000201.verbatim:
Dietary sugar loads (i.e. colas, apple juice, grape juice, honey, candy, sugar,
fructose, etc.) increase the natural rate of urinary Cr loss by 300 percent for
12 hours.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000202.claim_text: As part of a weight-loss plan, Wallach advises using a good weight-loss support product before each meal that contains pyruvate (fuel for the Krebs cycle), chromium picolinate, and chitosan, a saturated-fat binder. He describes chromium picolinate's role as allowing carbohydrate and fats to be burned. It is paired with pyruvate for energy metabolism and chitosan to bind fat.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000202.verbatim:
Use a good weight loss support product that contains pyruvate (fuel for
the Krebs Cycle, the body’s most basic metabolic process), chromium
picolinate (allows carbohydrate and fats to be burned), and chitosan (a
saturated fat binder) before each meal.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000203.claim_text: Wallach says cardiac arrhythmia can stem from deficiencies including B1 (beriberi), B3 (pellagra), B6, chromium, selenium, magnesium, potassium, carnitine and CoQ10. His treatment approach combines avoiding known allergens like MSG and sugar with a package of nutrients — including potassium at 500 mg three times a day, magnesium at 1,000 mg a day, plus selenium, chromium, B-complex, plant derived colloidal minerals, carnitine and CoQ10. Potassium is one specific piece of that broader arrhythmia protocol.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000203.verbatim:
Deficiencies that cause cardiac arrhythmia include B1 (i.e. beriberi), B3 (i.e.
pellagra), B6, chromium, selenium (i.e. Keshan Disease, cystic fibrosis),
magnesium, potassium, carnitine, and CO Q10.
Treatment of cardiac arrhythmia includes avoidance of known allergens
(MSG, sugar, etc.), autoimmune urine and blood therapies, chromium at 50-
100 mcg t.i.d., B-complex at 50 mg ti.d., selenium at 100-300 mcg t.i.d.,
magnesium at 1,000 mg/day, potassium at 500 mg ti.d., plant derived
colloidal minerals, carnitine, and CO Q10 per label.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000204.claim_text: Wallach notes that significant amounts of potassium are lost through vomiting. To counter this, he suggests drinking small volumes of an athletic fluid or electrolyte replacer, which helps restore what is lost. It is a practical example of how illness can rapidly deplete a mineral the body barely stores.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000204.verbatim:
Drinking small volumes of athletic fluid/ electrolyte
replacers is of value because significant amounts of potassium are lost
through vomiting.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000206.claim_text: Wallach cites Japanese research in which subjects were fed Chinese cabbage, turnips, buckwheat, noodles, a small amount of iodine, soybean, or seaweed, and goiter developed in every group except the seaweed eaters. He notes that goiter can even appear in Japanese living along the seacoast despite high daily iodine consumption. The takeaway is that iodine-rich seaweed stands out as a protective food where other foods did not prevent goiter.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000206.verbatim:
Goiter
develops in Japanese living along the seacoast despite high daily iodine
consumption. Japanese subjects being fed Chinese cabbage, turnips,
buckwheat, noodles, 2.0 mcg iodine, soybean, or seaweed developed goiter
in all groups except the seaweed eating group.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000207.claim_text: Wallach's treatment for goiter starts by removing all goitrogens from the diet, reading labels to exclude nitrates, then supplementing iodine at 250 mcg per day and thyroid USP at 2 to 5 grains each morning. He recommends kelp as a good natural source of iodine and reminds readers not to forget the 90 essential nutrients. The approach treats the underlying nutrient deficiency rather than only the swollen gland.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000207.verbatim:
Treatment of goiter includes the removal of all goitrogens from the diet
(read labels to exclude nitrates), supplement iodine at 250 mcg/day, and
thyroid USP at 2-5 grains each morning. Kelp is a good natural source of
iodine. Don’t forget the 90 essential nutrients.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000208.claim_text: Certain foods and additives are goitrogenic, meaning they stimulate goiter formation. Wallach flags nitrates found in luncheon meats, hot dogs, sausages, and other prepared meats, along with nitrates from fertilizer that seep into well water (which he warns are carcinogenic as well as goitrogenic). Cruciferous vegetables such as cabbage, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts are goitrogenic too, which is why treating goiter begins with stripping these from the diet.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000208.verbatim:
Nitrates are goiterogenic (stimulate goiter formation); they are found in
luncheon meats, hot dogs, sausages, and a variety of prepared meat
products. Another source of goiterogens is the nitrates in fertilizers, which
gets into well water. If you get your water from a farm well, have it tested
for nitrates because they are carcinogenic as well as goiterogenic. Cabbage,
broccoli, and Brussels sprouts are also goiterogenic.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000209.claim_text: According to Wallach, metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 mcg per day, giving a wide margin of safety. For comparison, the average American takes in only 170 to 250 mcg of iodine daily. He also notes that people lose a surprising amount, up to 146 mcg per day, through sweat with only moderate exercise, which can quietly deepen a shortfall.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000209.verbatim:
The average American takes in 170-250 mcg/day of iodine. Humans lose
considerable amounts of it in their sweat—up to 146 mcg/day with only
moderate exercise. Metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 mcg/day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000210.claim_text: Early in his veterinary career Wallach autopsied a flock of lambs that had died overnight with obvious goiter, their thyroid glands enlarged and their blood tinged chocolate. The farmer had dutifully provided iodine in a trace-mineral salt block, so iodine was not the problem. Wallach found the drought-stressed corn silage was heavy with nitrates, which act as a goitrogen that depresses thyroid activity and creates goiter even when iodine is present. The lambs had nitrate-induced hypothyroidism and could not control their body temperature on cool nights, and the case became his first peer-reviewed journal article.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000210.verbatim:
Nitrates act as a goitrogen, a
substance that depresses thyroid activity and creates a goiter, even when
iodine is present in the diet. All the lambs had nitrate-induced goiter and
hypothyroidism. They died during the cool fall nights, because they
couldn’t control their body temperature. This flock of lambs with nitrate-induced hypothyroidism became the subject of my first peer review,
refereed journal article. I was published!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000211.claim_text: Wallach explains that bruises form when a bump or blow ruptures blood vessels and releases blood into the surrounding tissue. He attributes the fragility and tenderness of capillaries that makes bruising easy to overdoses of blood thinners or to deficiencies of copper, vitamin K, vitamin C, or vitamin E. In other words, easy bruising can be a warning sign of inadequate vitamin E.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000211.verbatim:
BRUISES are the result of a bump or blow that ruptures blood vessels and
releases blood into the surrounding tissue including the skin. The fragility
(tenderness) of capillaries can result from overdoses of blood thinners,
copper deficiency, vitamin K, vitamin C, or vitamin E deficiencies.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000212.claim_text: Describing the nutritional awareness of the 1960s, Wallach notes that public attention was focused on vitamins. In that climate, Linus Pauling promoted vitamin C for preventing cancer, niacin was tied to schizophrenia, and vitamin E was touted for people's sex life and longevity. He presents this as a description of the era's vitamin enthusiasm rather than a clinical dosing claim.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000212.verbatim:
The nutritional awareness in humans during the sixties was focused on
vitamins. Theron Randolph emphasized the relationship between niacin
(B3) deficiency and schizophrenia. Linus Pauling promoted
vitamin C for preventing cancer. Vitamin E was touted for people’s sex life
and longevity.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000213.claim_text: Wallach says ecchymosis, or easy bruising, is very common — especially in women and children eating low-fiber, low-fruit, low-vegetable diets heavy in fast food, coffee, tea and soft drinks. His treatment includes alfalfa tablets, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, vitamin K at 15 mg/day, vitamin E at 800–1,200 IU/day, and 4–6 cups of green vegetables each day, while avoiding fried foods, margarine, sugar and caffeine.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000213.verbatim:
ECCHYMOSIS (easy bruising) is very common, especially in women and
children on low fiber, low fruit, and low vegetable diets (i.e. fast foods, lots
of coffee, tea, and soft drinks).
Treatment includes alfalfa tablets at 4-6 b.i.d., vitamin C to bowel tolerance,
vitamin K at 15 mg/day, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU/day, and 4-6 cups of
green vegetables each day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000214.claim_text: Wallach states that nosebleeds (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or vitamin C deficiencies, and he criticizes conventional ENT doctors for cauterizing the nasal capillaries instead of fixing the underlying cause. His approach is to raise vitamin K by eating more green leafy vegetables and reseeding the colon with Lactobacillus acidophilus — since those bacteria synthesize vitamin K — along with vitamin C to bowel tolerance. This treats the deficiency rather than just burning the vessels.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000214.verbatim:
NOSEBLEEDS (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or
vitamin C deficiencies. “Orthodox” EENTs like to do “minor” surgery on
noses to cauterize (i.e. burn) capillaries in the nasal membranes to stop the
nosebleeds. Treatment for nosebleeds should include increased
consumption of green leafy vegetables, reseeding the colon with
Lactobacillus acidophilus (the bacteria will synthesize vitamin K), vitamin
C to bowel tolerance,

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000215.claim_text: For seborrheic dermatitis - dandruff and cradle cap - Wallach recommends a combination protocol built around biotin at 100 mcg three times a day (t.i.d.). It also includes folic acid at 15-25 mg daily, B6 at 100 mg t.i.d., vitamin E at 800-1,200 mg/IU daily, essential fatty acids at 5 grams t.i.d., vitamin A at 300,000 IU daily as beta-carotene, zinc at 15 mg t.i.d., and Selsun Blue shampoo used topically. He notes that celiac-type intestinal lesions can drive the underlying malabsorption.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000215.verbatim:
Treatment of seborrheic dermatitis should include biotin at 100 mcg t.i.d.,
folic acid at 15-25 mg per day, B6 at 100 mg t.i.d., vitamin E at 800-1,200
mg IU per day, EFA at 5 grams ti.d., vitamin A at 300,000 IU per day as
beta-carotene, zinc at 15 mg t.i.d., and Selsun Blue shampoo topically.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000216.claim_text: Choline works together with vitamin B12/cobalt, folic acid and the amino acid methionine to transfer single carbon groups, known as methyl groups. These methyl transfers build the raw material to make RNA and to synthesize DNA from RNA, placing choline directly in the machinery of gene function.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000216.verbatim:
Vitamin B12/ cobalt joins
with folic acid, choline, and the amino acid methionine to transfer single
carbon groups (methyl groups) in the synthesis of the raw material to make
RNA and the synthesis of DNA from RNA.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000217.claim_text: In his Alzheimer's protocol Wallach recommends lecithin at 2,500 mg three times a day, calling it very useful at all stages of the disease. He adds that phosphatidyl choline is a more efficient form than plain lecithin.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000217.verbatim:
Lecithin at 2,500 mg t.i.d. is very useful at all
stages though phosphatidyl choline is more efficient.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000218.claim_text: For absence attacks (petit mal), a seizure type in which the patient briefly blinks and stops what they are doing before resuming, Wallach's treatment leads with choline at 4 grams per day. He pairs it with taurine, dimethyl glycine, phosphatidyl choline and vitamin B6.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000218.verbatim:
Treatment should
include choline 4 gm/day, taurine 500 mg t.i.d., dimethyl glycine 100 mg
b.i.d., phosphatidyl choline, and B6 100-300 mg/day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000219.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese and choline, not by a problem that requires surgery. His treatment supplies those minerals in plant-derived colloidal form along with vitamin B6 and zinc, the same nutrients he puts in his Pig Arthritis Formula, and he contrasts this directly with the orthodox approach of wrist surgery.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000219.verbatim:
Carpal tunnel
syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline.
Treatment includes B6 at 75 mg t.i.d., zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., plant derived
colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline. All of these nutrients are found
in Dr. Wallach’s Pig Arthritis Formula. Compare this with the “orthodox”
therapy of wrist surgery!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000220.claim_text: In Wallach's treatment protocol for cataracts, inositol is given at 150 mg/day as one component. It sits alongside avoiding fried foods and margarine, the base line vitamin/mineral supplement, vitamin E at 2,000 IU/day, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, the B vitamins, selenium, zinc, and several amino acids.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000220.verbatim:
Treatment of cataracts includes avoiding fried foods and margarine, the
base line vitamin/mineral supplement plus vitamin E at 2,000 IU/day,
vitamin C to bowel tolerance, B1, B2, B3, B5, and B6 at 50 mg b.i.d.,
inositol at 150 mg/day, selenium at 250 mcg/day, zinc at 25 mg
t.i.d.,

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000221.claim_text: In Wallach's treatment protocol for insomnia, vitamin B3 appears in two forms: niacinamide at 1,000 mg at bedtime, and time-release niacin (B3) at 450 mg three times a day. These sit within a broader sleep protocol that also uses calcium, chromium, tryptophan, inositol, and calming herbs such as valerian, passion flower, hops, and California poppy.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000221.verbatim:
niacinamide at 1,000 mg at bedtime, and herbs including valerian (Valeriana
officinalis), passion flower (Passiflora incarnata), hops (Humulus lupulus), and California poppy
(Eschscholzia California), and B3 (niacin) at 450 mg t.i.d. (time release).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000222.claim_text: Wallach describes vanadium as an essential trace mineral, proven essential in 1971, whose central job is handling blood sugar. It stimulates glucose oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen synthesis in the liver and muscle, while inhibiting the liver's own production of glucose and the gut's absorption of it, and it heightens insulin's effect. Because it behaves so much like insulin—making cell insulin receptors more sensitive—Wallach treats vanadium, paired with chromium, as a cornerstone mineral for hypoglycemia, obesity, and adult-onset (type 2) diabetes, which he regards not as a genetic disease but as a simple chromium-and-vanadium deficiency.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000222.verbatim:
Vanadium was proven to be essential in 1971. Vanadium stimulates blood
sugar (glucose) oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen (animal
starch) synthesis in liver and muscle, and inhibits liver gluconeogenesis
(production of glucose from fat) and absorption of glucose from the gut.
Vanadium enhances the stimulating effect of insulin on DNA synthesis.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000224.claim_text: Wallach says the form of vanadium determines how much the body can absorb. Metallic vanadium (vanadyl sulfate) is absorbed from the intestinal tract very poorly, at only 0.1 to 1.0 percent. Vanadium chelates are absorbed at 40 percent, while plant-derived colloidal forms are absorbed at up to 98 percent.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000224.verbatim:
Metallic vanadium (vanadyl
sulfate) is absorbed from the intestinal tract very poorly at only 0.1 to 1.0
percent, vanadium chelates are absorbed at 40 percent, and plant derived
colloidal forms at up to 98 percent.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000225.claim_text: Wallach identifies chromium and vanadium as the 'magic bullets' for treating hypoglycemia, at 50 to 200 mcg three times a day with meals. He warns that people already on insulin should start chromium/vanadium therapy at a lower 25 mcg three times a day to prevent a sudden dip in blood sugar. He also notes that simple sugars can increase the urinary excretion of chromium and vanadium up to 300 percent of the normal rate.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000225.verbatim:
Chromium and vanadium
are the “magic bullets” for treatment of hypoglycemia at 50-200 mcg t.i.d.
with meals. THOSE INDIVIDUALS ON INSULIN SHOULD START
CHROMIUM / VANADIUM THERAPY AT 25 mcg ti.d. TO PREVENT A
SUDDEN DIP IN BLOOD SUGAR.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000226.claim_text: Wallach lists the clinical diseases associated with vanadium deficiency: slow growth, increased infant mortality, infertility, elevated cholesterol and triglycerides, hypoglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, narcolepsy, prediabetes, diabetes, ADD/ADHD, depression, manic depression (bipolar disease), Tourette's syndrome, cardiovascular disease, and obesity.

Clinical Diseases Associated with Vanadium Deficiency
Slow growth

ADD, ADHD

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000229.claim_text: Germanium is known to enhance the immune system. It does this by stimulating the production of natural killer cells, lymphokines such as interferon, macrophages, and T-suppressor cells -- the cells the body uses to defend against infection and abnormal cells.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000229.verbatim:
Germanium is known to enhance the
immune system by stimulating production of natural killer cells,
lymphokines such as IFN(y) interferon, macrophages, and T-suppresser
cells.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000230.claim_text: GE-132 is the organic germanium compound at the center of germanium's supplement story. Wallach recounts that Dr. Asai synthesized it — carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide — in 1967 by a hydrolysis method, giving a cubic molecular structure with three negatively charged oxygen ions at its base. As an organic (chelated) form it is absorbed at about 30 percent efficiency and the entire intake clears the body within a week. He adds that ordinary food plants and animals carry only traces of germanium (beans about 4.67 ppm, tuna 2.3 ppm), while prized healing herbs — and even the famed waters of Lourdes — are unusually rich in it.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000230.verbatim:
Asai synthesized GE-132, carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide, in 1967 by
a hydrolysis method. This organic germanium structure forms a cubic
structure with three negative oxygen ions at the base of a cubic triangle. As
an organic or chelate form of germanium, GE-132 is absorbed at the rate of
30 percent efficiency and the total intake is excreted in one week.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000231.claim_text: Germanium is found in significant amounts in plants like Shiitake mushrooms, ginseng, and garlic. It works by increasing oxygen flow into cells from the blood -- and cancer cells do not like high levels of oxygen -- while boosting macrophage activity, antibody-forming cells, T-cells, B-lymphocytes, and killer cells, and inducing the body to produce interferon. Wallach says it can be used either as prevention or in cancer therapy programs.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000231.verbatim:
GERMANIUM is found in significant amounts in a variety of plants
including imported Shiitake mushrooms, ginseng, garlic, etc. Germanium
functions by increasing the oxygen flow into cells from the blood (cancer
cells do not like high levels of
oxygen), increases macrophage (scavenger cells) activity, increases the
numbers of antibody forming cells, T-cells, B-lymphocytes, and killer cells,
and induces the body to produce interferon! This can be used as prevention
or in therapy programs.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000232.claim_text: In Wallach's Alzheimer's protocol, treatment includes germanium given intramuscularly -- 5 ml of standard solution every other day for 24 days -- followed by oral germanium at 150 mg twice daily (b.i.d.), alongside the baseline nutritional supplements.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000232.verbatim:
Treatment should include germanium IM 5 ml of standard solution every
other day for 24 days followed by oral germanium at 150 mg b.i.d.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000233.claim_text: In 1950 the Japanese chemist Dr. Kazuhiko Asai found traces of germanium in fossilized plant life — the start of a long line of research into the element's healing role. Russian researchers soon attributed anti-cancer activity to germanium, and Asai went on to connect the healing reputation of certain herbs to their unusually high germanium content; many prized medicinal herbs turn out to be germanium 'accumulator' plants. Wallach frames germanium as a semiconductor-like element that helps move electrons inside cells and aids oxygen use, and credits it with stimulating immune defenders such as natural killer cells and interferon.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000233.verbatim:
In 1950, Dr. Kazuhiko Asai, a Japanese chemist, found traces of germanium
in fossilized plant life. Russian researchers quickly attributed anti-cancer
activity to germanium. Dr. Asai was able to connect the healing properties
of certain herbs to relatively high levels of germanium. Many of these herbs
are germanium accumulator plants.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000234.claim_text: Wallach states that in children, manganese and/or tin deficiency can cause reversible hearing loss, meaning the hearing can return once the deficiency is corrected. He also advises a pulse test for milk allergies, another common cause of deafness in kids. The message is that childhood hearing loss is often nutritional and fixable rather than permanent.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000234.verbatim:
In children, manganese and/or tin deficiency can cause
reversible hearing loss. Do a pulse test for milk allergies (another common
cause of deafness in kids).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000235.claim_text: Wallach holds that carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline. His treatment includes vitamin B6 at 75 mg three times a day, zinc at 50 mg three times a day, and plant-derived colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline, all nutrients found in his Pig Arthritis Formula. He contrasts this nutritional approach with the orthodox therapy of wrist surgery.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000235.verbatim:
Carpal tunnel
syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline.
Treatment includes B6 at 75 mg t.i.d., zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., plant derived
colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline. All of these nutrients are found
in Dr. Wallach’s Pig Arthritis Formula. Compare this with the “orthodox”
therapy of wrist surgery!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000236.claim_text: In Wallach's approach to epilepsy, manganese at 50 mg per day is among the indicated nutrients, together with zinc at 50 mg three times a day, essential fatty acids at 5 gm three times a day, choline at 4 gm/day, taurine at 500 mg three times a day, and dimethyl glycine at 100 mg twice a day. Because convulsions are one of the classic manganese-deficiency signs, correcting the mineral is part of resolving the seizures. This nutritional protocol is offered as an alternative to standard anticonvulsant drugs.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000236.verbatim:
Manganese at 50 mg/day, zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., essential fatty
acids at 5 gm t.i.d., choline at 4 gm/day, taurine at 500 mg t.i.d., and
dimethyl glycine at 100 mg b.i.d. are also indicated.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000237.claim_text: Wallach makes the provocative claim that repetitive stress and repetitive motion syndrome are manganese-deficiency problems rather than mere mechanical injuries. In his words, we see literally millions of people at work with Velcro wrist, neck, elbow, finger, knee, back, and hip supports — all for manganese deficiencies.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000237.verbatim:
We see
literally millions of people at work with Velcro wrist, neck, elbow, finger,
knee, back, and hip supports—all for manganese deficiencies!!!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000239.claim_text: Wallach describes an enterohepatic circulation - a direct intestine-to-liver loop - that recycles vitamin B12 from bile and other intestinal secretions. This recycling is why a B12 deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after they give up meat.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000239.verbatim:
There is an enterohepatic (intestine direct to the
liver) circulation of Vitamin B12 that recycles B12 from bile and other
intestinal secretions which explains why B12 deficiency in vegans may not
appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000240.claim_text: For ADD and ADHD, Wallach insists treatment must include complete removal of alcohol and sugar, natural and processed, from the diet, and teaching the person the connection between sugar and their behavior — with the whole family eating the same way. He names plant-derived colloidal lithium, chromium and vanadium as the specific supplements to take, adding that it is best to take all 90 essential nutrients.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000240.verbatim:
Treatment must include complete removal of alcohol and sugar (natural and
processed) from the diet and educating the ADD/ADHD victim that there is
a connection between sugar consumption and their negative behavior. The
whole family must eat the same way if this dietary approach is to be
successful! Plant derived colloidal lithium, chromium, and vanadium are
specific supplements to be taken. It is best to take all 90 essential nutrients.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000241.claim_text: Wallach describes goiter (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) as being caused by a simple deficiency of nutrients, and he includes molybdenum in that list alongside iodine, copper, and the amino acid tyrosine. In his framework the enlarged thyroid gland is a sign of these underlying nutrient deficiencies.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000241.verbatim:
GOITER (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) is caused by a simple deficiency of
nutrients (i.e. iodine, copper, molybdenum, the amino acid tyrosine, etc.).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000242.claim_text: Wallach explains that the balance of sodium, potassium, and chloride is controlled by the adrenal cortex hormones and the anterior pituitary gland. Addison's disease — a loss of adrenal cortex function — causes loss of sodium and impaired potassium retention, producing general weakness, muscle cramps, weight loss, and a marked 'salt hunger.' He notes these symptoms can be relieved by supplementing with sodium chloride or by giving adrenal cortical hormones.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000242.verbatim:
Addison’s
Disease, a loss of function of the adrenal cortex,
results in the loss of Na and K retention with clinical signs of general
weakness, muscle cramps, weight loss, and a marked “salt hunger.” The
symptoms can be relieved with the supplementation of NaCl or by
administering adrenal cortical hormones.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000243.claim_text: Wallach defines pica — cribbing and cravings for things like dirt, paint, snack food, sugar, and salt — as a symptom of one or more nutritional mineral deficiencies, insisting that only mineral deficiencies cause this behavior. In adults it shows up as cravings for ice, chips, salsa, chocolate, and soft drinks; in children as eating dirt or paint chips. His remedy is mineral supplementation, including plant-derived colloidal minerals, rather than willpower.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000243.verbatim:
PICA (cribbing, cravings for dirt, paint, snack food, sugar, salt, etc.) is a
symptom of one or more nutritional mineral deficiencies. Only mineral
deficiencies cause this pica behavior. Adults often evidence pica when
they crave ice, chips, salsa, chocolate, and soft drinks. Children evidence
pica when they eat dirt and/or paint chips.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000244.claim_text: During the 1993 heat wave, Wallach says the cause of the thousands of American casualties was a simple salt (sodium) deficiency — basic heat stroke that, in his words, any boy scout could diagnose and remedy with water and salt. He states that almost all of those who died were on salt-restricted diets prescribed by their physicians, making it a physician-caused disaster. Those who were successfully treated, he notes, were given IV saline — salt water.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000244.verbatim:
I knew the
horrible toll of the heat wave was the result of a simple salt or sodium
deficiency. It was basic heat stroke that any boy scout could diagnose,
recognize, and remedy with water and salt. Yes, the cause of these
thousands of American casualties was a simple salt deficiency. Almost all
of those who died during the heat wave were on salt restricted diets. It was a
physician-caused disaster.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000245.claim_text: Wallach teaches that pregnancy toxemia (eclampsia) results from the low-protein, low-salt diets some women adopt in an attempt to prevent excess weight gain during pregnancy. In his framework, cutting salt during pregnancy is a cause of the problem, not a way to prevent it.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000245.verbatim:
PREGNANCY TOXEMIA (eclampsia) is the result of low protein, low
salt diets entered into in an attempt to prevent excess weight gain in
pregnancy.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000246.claim_text: Wallach calls phosphorus an extremely important essential mineral that gets little attention from nutritionists only because it is so widely available in food. It is a major structural mineral of the bones and teeth and, he says, has more functions in the human body than any other mineral: a vital constituent of nucleic acids (DNA), an activator of enzymes, and a driver of several steps of the adenosine triphosphate (ATP) energy cycle and red-blood-cell metabolism. Second only to calcium in abundance, it makes up about 22 percent of the body's total mineral content, and Wallach notes that a complete discussion of phosphorus would require a discussion of every metabolic function in the body.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000246.verbatim:
Phosphorus is an extremely important essential mineral, however, it
gets little or no attention from nutritionists because it is widely available in
all foods. Phosphorus is a major structural mineral for bones and teeth. It
has more functions in the human than any other mineral including its role as
a vital constituent of nucleic acids, activating enzymes, and for several steps
of the ATP energy cycle, RBC metabolism.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000247.claim_text: Wallach states that phosphorus is second in abundance only to calcium in the human body, making up 22 percent of the body's total mineral content. The body contains about 800 grams of phosphorus, just short of two pounds, of which 700 grams sits in the bones and teeth as insoluble calcium phosphate. The rest circulates as biologically active phosphorus combined with carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and other compounds.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000247.verbatim:
Second
in abundance only to calcium in the human body, it comprises 22 percent of
the body’s total mineral content. The human body contains about 800 grams
of P, just short of two pounds, of which 700 grams is found in bones and
teeth as insoluble calcium phosphate.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000248.claim_text: Beyond its structural role, Wallach explains that the phosphorus not stored in bone circulates as biologically active colloidal phosphorus bound to carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and other compounds, including the blood's major buffer system. Critically, he says the B-complex vitamins function as coenzymes in intracellular metabolism only when combined with phosphorus — making phosphorus a required partner for the whole B-vitamin family to do its work.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000248.verbatim:
The balance of P in the human body is found as biologically active intra and
extracellular colloidal P in combination with carbohydrates, lipids, protein,
and a wide variety of other biologically active organic compounds including
the blood’s major buffer system. B-complex vitamins function as
coenzymes to intracellular metabolic functions only when combined with
phosphorus.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000249.claim_text: Wallach puts the average adult dietary intake of phosphorus at 1,000 to 1,500 mg per day. Absorption depends heavily on form: metallic phosphorus is limited to about three to five percent in adults and older children (up to 8-12 percent in infants), mixed chelated dietary sources reach 40 to 50 percent, and organically bound colloidal phosphorus is absorbed up to 98 percent. He adds that optimal absorption of metallic and chelated phosphorus occurs when the dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio is 1:1.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000249.verbatim:
The average adult human dietary intake of P is 1,000 to 1,500 mg/day. In
adults and older children, the absorption of metallic P is limited to about
three to five per cent and as high as eight to 12 percent in infants. Mixed
dietary sources of chelated P may be absorbed at the rate of 40 to 50
percent. Optimal absorption of metallic and chelated P occurs when the
dietary Ca:P ratio is 1:1. Organically bound colloidal P is absorbed up to 98
percent.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000250.claim_text: Wallach says a dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio of 2:1 is ideal yet impossible to attain on an unsupplemented diet. The calcium-to-phosphorus ratios of everyday foods are consistently and wildly off: grain 1:8, red meat 1:12, fish 1:12, carbonated drinks 1:8, and organ meat (liver, kidney) as extreme as 1:44. None of these are anywhere near correct, so they increase calcium loss from the body, bones and teeth — meaning the more meat you eat, the more calcium supplementation you need.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000250.verbatim:
The calcium/phosphorus ratios of
food items is consistent: FOOD CALCIUM PHOSPHORUS
grain 1 8
red meat 1 12
organ meat 1 44
(liver, kidney)
fish 1 12
carbonated drinks 1 8
It is easily seen that none of the calcium/phosphorus ratios of the basic
foods are anywhere near correct. These increase the calcium loss from the
body including the bones and teeth. The more meat you eat, the more
calcium supplementation you need.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000251.claim_text: Wallach explains that phosphorus is present as phytates in cereals and whole grain flours. When bread is made from unleavened flours, the phytic acid complexes with calcium, iron, zinc and other minerals in the gut, further lowering their absorption rate. This is why phosphorus in grain form can work against the very minerals the body needs.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000251.verbatim:
Phosphorus is
present as phytates in cereals and whole grain flours, therefore, if bread is
made from unleavened flours, the phytic acid will complex with Ca, Fe, Zn,
and other minerals further lowering their absorption rate.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000252.claim_text: Wallach notes that phosphorus deficiency has long been recognized in livestock — where its signs include pica, cribbing and fractures — but has only recently been recognized in humans. Because phosphorus underlies so many biological functions, its deficiency is widespread, universal and ultimately fatal, largely through a decrease in adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis that amounts to complete metabolic energy failure. The result carries associated neuromuscular, skeletal, blood and kidney disease.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000252.verbatim:
Deficiencies of P have long been recognized in livestock. Symptoms of P
deficiency include the behavior of pica and cribbing and fractures.
Phosphorus deficiency has only recently been recognized in humans. The
widespread, universal, and ultimately fatal results of P deficiency are the
result of its widespread biological functions, significantly as the result of a
decrease in ATP synthesis (complete metabolic energy failure) with
associated neuromuscular, skeletal, blood, and kidney disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000253.claim_text: Wallach's distinctive position is that the correct dietary ratio is 2 parts calcium to 1 part phosphorus, but most American diets are inverted to 15-20 parts phosphorus per 1 part calcium. He treats gum and jaw disease as osteoporosis of the face and jaw, driven by this imbalance. Correcting it is impossible without supplementing calcium and consciously cutting phosphorus — giving up soft drinks and reducing meat intake.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000253.verbatim:
The correct calcium/phosphorus ratio is 2 calcium/1
phosphorus (most American diets are 15-20 phosphorus/ 1 calcium) and it
is impossible to achieve without supplementation of calcium and
consciously reducing the phosphorus intake (i.e. give up soft drinks, reduce
meat intake, etc.).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000254.claim_text: Wallach cites LeVaillant's 1796 description of 'phosphate appetite' — the anxious search by cattle in phosphate-deficient South African pastures for discarded animal bones, a behavior called osteophagia. Phosphorus-deficient cattle also chewed on wood and each other's horns. He notes this bone-chewing has been reported across many wild herbivore species, including reindeer, caribou, red deer, camels, giraffe, elephant and wildebeest.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000254.verbatim:
Phosphate appetite was described by LeVaillant (1796) as the anxious
search by cattle in phosphate deficient South African pastures for discarded
animal bones (osteophagia). Phosphorous deficient cattle also chewed on
wood and each others horns.
Osteophagia has been reported in many wild species of herbivores
including reindeer, caribou, red deer, camels, giraffe, elephant, and
wildebeest.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000255.claim_text: Wallach lists the sulfur-containing proteins that work in indirect ways to keep you alive: hemoglobin, hormones (including insulin and the adrenal cortical hormones), enzymes, and antibodies. Sulfur also turns up in carbohydrates such as heparin, a natural anticoagulant concentrated in the liver, and in chondroitin sulfate, a component of cartilage. Even the vitamins thiamine (B1) and biotin carry sulfur bound in their molecules.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000255.verbatim:
Sulfur-containing proteins work in indirect ways to maintain life:
• Hemoglobin
• Hormones (insulin, adrenal cortical hormones) • Enzymes • Antibodies
Sulfur also occurs in carbohydrates such as heparin, an anticoagulant that is
concentrated in the liver and other tissues, and chondroitin sulfate
(cartilage, gelatin). The vitamins thiamine (B1) and biotin have S bound in
their molecule.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000256.claim_text: Wallach treats the fingernails as barometers of absorption and nutritional status. Brittle nails, in his reading, point to sulfur amino acid and protein deficiencies, while white spots signal zinc deficiency and ridges can indicate iron or calcium deficiency. He advises correcting the underlying nutrition, including the base-line supplements, rather than treating the nail alone.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000256.verbatim:
FINGERNAILS (white spots, ridges, brittle) are good barometers of
absorption and nutritional status. Bluish fingernails indicate chronic lung
conditions (i.e. not enough oxygen); white spots indicate zinc deficiency;
ridges can indicate iron and/or calcium deficiency; brittle nails indicates
sulfur amino acid and protein deficiencies.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000257.claim_text: According to Wallach, foul bowel gas usually comes from digested but poorly absorbed food reaching the colon, where bowel organisms ferment it. Food sensitivities to wheat, gluten, and dairy can trigger celiac-type changes in the small intestine that cause this malabsorption. The unabsorbed proteins then reach the colon and become the source of the sulfur that smells like rotten eggs.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000257.verbatim:
FARTING (bowel gas) is usually caused by digested but poorly absorbed
food reaching the colon and being fermented by bowel organisms. Some
foods such as beans, garlic, and onions are legendary for their production of
bowel gas. Food sensitivities to wheat, wheat gluten, and dairy can cause
celiac disease type changes in the small intestine, which results in
malabsorption. The unabsorbed proteins reach the colon and are the source
of sulfur that smells like rotten eggs.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000260.claim_text: Wallach rejects the orthodox view that systemic lupus erythematosus is fundamentally an autoimmune disease in which the body attacks itself. He argues the autoimmune defect appears as a result of the disease and of abnormal proteins, rather than being its cause. Characteristically present, he says, are multiple mineral deficiencies of sulfur, copper, selenium, and others.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000260.verbatim:
The “orthodox” theory is that
SLE is an “autoimmune” disease that causes the patient’s own antibodies to
attack themselves. The fact is the autoimmune defect occurs as a result of
the disease and the presence of abnormal proteins rather than being the
cause. Multiple mineral deficiencies of sulfur, copper, selenium, etc. are
characteristically present.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000261.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, chloride is essential to every living species — it drives electrochemical and catalytic reactions and activates numerous enzymes. He groups it with sodium and potassium as one of three indispensable electrolytes that govern water balance, osmotic equilibrium, acid-base balance, and muscular function. Its single most important role, though, is serving as the basic raw material the stomach uses to manufacture hydrochloric acid (HCl) — the stomach acid that digests protein via pepsin, activates intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption, and lets the body absorb minerals. Ordinary table salt (sodium chloride) is the universal source of chloride ions.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000261.verbatim:
Chlorine is essential for all living species’ electrochemical and catalytic
functions, activates numerous enzymes, and is the basic raw material for
our stomachs to make stomach acid (HCl) for protein digestion by pepsin,
B12 absorption (intrinsic factor activation), and absorption of minerals.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000263.claim_text: Wallach groups sodium, chlorine, and potassium as three indispensable electrolytes so intimately associated that they are presented together. By his figures sodium makes up two percent, potassium five percent, and chlorine three percent of the body's total mineral content, with sodium and chloride living mainly outside the cells (extracellular) and potassium inside them. Together the three run at least four physiological jobs: maintaining normal water balance and distribution, osmotic equilibrium, acid-base balance, and muscular irritability.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000263.verbatim:
Sodium, chlorine, and potassium are three indispensable “electrolytes” so
intimately associated in the body that they can be presented together.
Sodium makes up two percent, potassium five percent, and chlorine three
percent of the total mineral content of the human body. All three are widely
distributed throughout the body tissues and fluids, however, Na and CI are
primarily extracellular (outside the cell), while K is an intracellular (inside
the cell) mineral. Sodium, potassium, and chlorine are involved in at least
four important physiological functions in the body: 1. Maintenance of
normal water balance and distribution.
2. Maintenance of normal osmotic equilibrium.
3. Maintenance of normal acid-base balance.
4. Maintenance of normal muscular irritability.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000264.claim_text: Wallach describes the sweat test as a nonspecific test that measures the amount of electrolytes—sodium, chlorides, and potassium—in sweat. Though originally thought to be a specific genetic indicator for cystic fibrosis, he says it is now known to be positive in 17 different diseases plus food allergies, starvation, kwashiorkor, and celiac disease. He attributes the mechanism to essential fatty acid deficiencies and the resulting lack of prostaglandins that control sweat electrolyte levels in the skin.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000264.verbatim:
SWEAT TEST a nonspecific test that measures the amount of electrolytes
(i.e. sodium, chlorides, and potassium) in sweat. Originally it was thought
to be a specific genetic indicator for cystic fibrosis (CF). However, today it
has been found to be positive in 17 different diseases, food allergies,
starvation, kwashiorkor, celiac disease, etc. The mechanism is related to
EFA deficiencies and thus the lack of certain prostaglandins (short-lived
hormone-like substances) which control sweat electrolyte levels in the skin.
